RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the October 24, 2008/Kartika 2, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
35
Import of pulses
*101. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
CONSUMER AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government has recently
decided to import pulses from foreign
countries to augment domestic availability
and to check its rising prices;
(b) if so, the details thereof and under
what terms and conditions such imports of
pulses have been allowed;
(c) whether the indigenous production
of pulses has fallen in the past few years;
(d) if so, the factors responsible for fall
in production of pulses; and
(e) the steps taken by Government to
encourage production of pulses in the
country and to avoid its import?
Import of pulses by Public Sector
institutions
†*102 SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that pulses have
been imported by public sector institutions
to meet the demand of pulses by consumers
and control their prices in the country;
(b) if so, the names of the institutions
which have imported pulses and the
quantity of pulses imported by them in
the years 2005, 2006, 2007 and till
September, 2008;
(c) the average cost of each pulse after
its import in India during the said period;
and
(d) the cost at which imported pulses
were sold by these institutions in the
country?
Railway projects in the North Eastern
Region
*103. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the length of railways in the whole
of the country and that in the North-Eastern
States;

36
(b) the length of the broad-gauge and
metre-gauge railway lines in the different
States of the country;
(c) the details of status of gauge
conversion in the North-Eastern States; and
(d) the status of construction of new
lines in the North-Eastern States?
Rottening of grains in FCI godowns
†*104. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister  of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the quantity of grains rotted in the
godowns of Food Corporation of India
during the period 2005 to September, 2008;
(b) the market price of the rotted grains
together with the amount that had to be
spent to lift the same;
(c) the reasons for the rottening of
grains alongwith the names of the officers
found responsible for it; and
(d) the steps taken to ensure non-
rottening of grains in the godowns of Food
Corporation of India in future?
Health scenario in the country
*105. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA:
SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI:
Will the Minister  of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the details of programmes being
implemented under the National Rural
Health Mission in the country;
(b) the targets fixed for 2007-08 and the
achievements thereof, alongwith the details
in respect of Rajasthan;
(c) the status of health scenario in the
country, programme-wise and where
Rajasthan stands in this regard; and
(d) in what manner various national
parameters of rural health in the country
compare with the developing and
developed countries?
Absorption of porters/coolies as fourth
grade employees
*106. SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister  of RAILW AYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
has decided that porters/coolies would be
absorbed as fourth grade employees;
(b) if so, whether they would be given
the scale of fourth grade employees; and
(c) if so, whether passengers would not
be required to pay porters/coolies?
Deficit in rainfall in certain areas
*107. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister  of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Peninsular
India was facing deficit in rainfall from
South-West Monsoon during the period
15 June—15 July;
(b) if so, whether there are areas where
deficit has been more than 40 per cent and
whether in those areas there has been no
sowing or the seeds sown have not
germinated;
(c) whether the situation was aggravated
by the very poor prospects of monsoon rains
reviving in these areas before August; and
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

37
(d) if so, whether Government has sent
teams to the affected States to assess the
‘scarcity’ conditions prevalent and to make
an estimate of relief funds that would be
needed to tackle the emergency?
Suicides by farmers despite the
packages
*108. SHRI MOINUL HASSAN: Will
the Minister  of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether attention of Government
has been drawn to the CAG report on
"Farmers Packages" in Maharashtra and the
performance audit the Government of
Maharashtra presented to the Assembly;
(b) whether Government is aware that
the CAG report says, ‘‘No evaluation of
the implementation of the packages, in
terms of reduction in agrarian distress, was
made";
(c) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto; and
(d) despite the State Government's
Rs. 1075 crore "package" for farmers and
after the Prime Minister's visit in mid 2006
and the Central Government's Rs. 3750
crore package, how the incidents of suicides
continued unabated?
Diversion of foodgrains meant for
flood relief
†*109. SHRI ALI ANWAR ANSARI:
SHRI RAJNITI PRASAD:
Will the Minister  of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that instead of
distributing among beneficiaries, thousands
of quintals of rice and wheat made available
as a nutritional food and flood relief measure
by Central Government, for the years
2002-03, 2003-04, and 2004-05, was sold
in black market in Khutauna and Laukahi
blocks of Madhubani district in Bihar;
and
(b) if so, the details thereof?
Reduction in production capacity of
FACT
†*110. SHRI BALA V ANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister  of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the production capacity of
Fertilizers and Chemicals, Travancore
Limited has gone down in the current year
since the year 2004;
(b) the amount of fall in production
capacity;
(c) whether reservations thereto have
been expressed by the Comptroller and
Auditor General; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Salient features of the Rashtriya
Krishi Vikas Yojana
*111. SHRI N.K. SINGH: Will the
Minister  of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) the main features of the Special
Agricultural Plan under the Rashtriya Krishi
Vikas Yojana; and
(b) the progress made so far in the
implementation of the plan?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

38
Gas-based fertilizer plants in Uttar
Pradesh
*112. SHRI MAHENDRA MOHAN :
Will the Minister  of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) with the huge discovery of natural
gas in the Krishna-Godavari and Mahanadi
basin, whether his Ministry has planned a
roadmap for establishing gas based fertilizer
plants in the country;
(b) whether any study has been
undertaken to convert coal/Nafta based
fertilizer plants into gas-based fertilizer
plants to make them economically viable;
(c) if so, the details in this regard; and
(d) how many such plants will be
established in Uttar Pradesh?
Bypassing of Dental Council of India
*113. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister  of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE  be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
had granted permission to a large number
of dental colleges to conduct post-graduate
courses in surgery  bypassing or
disregarding the views of Dental Council
of India;
(b) if so, what are the number of such
Dental Colleges which have been given
permission for post-graduate courses in
surgery;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
recommendation of  Dental Council of India
is necessary for admission of students in
dental colleges, including post-graduate
courses in dental surgery; and
(d) if so, under which rule Government
has flouted this mandatory provision?
Contaminated drinking water
*114. SHRI RAJEEV
CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister
of HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
increasing health hazards posed by unsafe/
contaminated drinking water with high
levels of heavy metals and pesticides used
by farmers in many cities and States; and
(b) if so, the steps Government
proposes to take to address this issue?
Implementation of new food labelling
rules
*115. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister  of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
defer implementation of new food labelling
rules by another three months;
(b) whether Ministry had issued a draft
notification regarding food labelling which
was to be implemented by May 20,  2008;
(c) if so, whether Government has now
decided to defer its implementation; and
(d) what are main reasons therefor and
by when a final decision in this regard is
likely to be taken?
Train protection warning system
*116. MS. MABEL REBELLO:
SHRI B.J. PANDA:
 Will the Minister  of RAILW AYS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is proposed to launch
train protection warning system, that will

39
eliminate human error  i.e. signal passing at
danger and over-speeding, etc.;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether this system has since been
tested successfully and installed on certain
sections of the Indian Railways;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) what is the time-frame within which
it would be installed on East Coast Railway
and other Rail systems?
Cultivation of pulses
†*117. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister  of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the area in which pulses are generally
cultivated across the country;
(b) the area which is estimated to come
under the cultivation of pulses during Kharif
session in the year 2008-09;
(c) whether it is a fact that this year
pulses have been cultivated only in 65 per
cent area which would result in the shortage
of at least 10 lakh tonnes in the production
of pulses;
(d) whether it is also a fact that pulse
sector has been overlooked in Green
Revolution and its production is still
stagnating at subsistence level; and
(e) whether there is any scheme under
consideration to meet the scarcity?
Procurement of wheat
*118. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister  of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has procured
wheat from the farmers/markets during the
current rabi season for distribution under
PDS;
(b) if so, the total quantum of wheat
procured and at what cost;
(c) whether the policy of
Government to supply wheat to State
Governments under PDS has been
modified; and
(d) if so, to what extent Government
ensures that the wheat supplied to State
Governments under PDS is properly
utilized?
Utilization of non-productive animals
†*119.  SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI BALA V ANT ALIAS
BAL APTE:
Will the Minister  of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) the State-wise details of milching
and non-productive animals;
(b) whether any survey has been
conducted to use these non-productive
animals for carrying load alongwith the
State-wise percentage thereof;
(c) whether Government encourages the
efforts to generate income by producing
manure, medicines, pesticides by using the
excreta of non-milching animals;
(d) if so, the State-wise details thereof;
and
(e) whether such per animal average
income is being considered sufficient for
subsistence of their remaining period of life?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

40
Deaths due to non-communicable
diseases
*120. SHRI JESUDASU SEELAM:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI REDDY:
Will the Minister  of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether a report jointly prepared
by World Health Organisation and World
Economic Forum has pointed out that the
number of people dying from non-
communicable diseases is likely to rise to
47 million a year in the next 25 years;
(b) if so, whether life style diseases
would cost India 237 billion  dollars by
2012;
(c) whether according to this report, the
developed countries would be the worst
hit;
(d) whether Government has considered
the report; and
(e) if so, what are the steps being
considered by his Minsitry in this regard?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 18th October, 2008 Secretary-General.
Asvina 26, 1930 (Saka)

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Agriculture :  107, 108, 111, 117, 119,
Chemicals and Fertilizers : 110, 112,
Consumer Affairs, Food and Public
Distribution : 101, 102, 104, 109, 118,
Health and Family Welfare : 105, 113, 114, 115, 120,
Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises :—
Railways : 103, 106, 116.
Steel :—
GMGIPMRND—3348RS—18.10.2008.
